That is a 4-day-old newborn with a one-day history of generalized rash, born at term after maternal gonorrhea treated years ago. Is there any purulent discharge from the eyes or nose, or is the baby feeding well?

The Gram stain was negative for gonococcal meningitis. To further evaluate this generalized rash in a 4-day-old, does the infant have any jaundice, lethargy, or poor feeding, and has the mother received any prenatal care or vaccinations?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work and serology results are normal, which rules out sepsis and common congenital infections. Given the 4-day age and generalized rash, are there any vesicles or pustules present, and has the baby been touching anyone with cold sores or shingles?

The close-up images of the rash are required to determine if the lesions are vesicular or pustular, as the current normal blood work rules out sepsis and common congenital infections. Please provide the detailed images of the rash.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Erythema Toxicum (Note: While the description of pustules and sparing of palms/soles strongly suggests this, the presence of true pustules in a 4-day-old with a history of untreated maternal gonorrhea raises a differential for disseminated gonococcal infection or early HSV; however, given the negative Gram stain and normal blood work, Erythema Toxicum is the most likely clinical diagnosis fitting the "sparing of palms and soles" description).
